rows.n: Customs data record 0.893 Mt of coke and semi-coke exported from Zimbabwe in 2024 (CEPII BACI, HS 2704), 2.7% of the world total. The EIA table of metallurgical coke production on the Metallurgical coal page gives Zimbabwe no coke production in 2025 (its series reads 0 in 2025, and its last two years with production are 399 kt in 2022 and 5 kt in 2023; EIA International Energy Data). Two readings fit, with the same weight: the EIA series no longer covers the country's coke plants (a series that falls from 399 kt to 5 kt and then to nothing may be a series that stopped), or part of these tonnes is another product declared under the coke code, metallurgical coal for instance, of which the EIA tables of the Metallurgical coal page give Zimbabwe a production of 1.25 Mt in 2025 and no exports. Neither is established here.

flowDefs: Australia rows are Queensland only: producers' sales to export of hard coking, semi-soft coking and PCI coal together, by first destination.
United States rows are exports of rank metallurgical as declared, by first destination.
notes: Coke and semi-coke (HS 270400, customs data), 2024 (CEPII BACI): world 32.92 Mt gross weight; top exporters China 8.59 Mt, Poland 5.23 Mt, Indonesia 5.22 Mt. The tables of customs coke follow the EIA tables of metallurgical coke: the two sources differ in what they count (EIA's coke is metallurgical coke by country; HS 2704 is every coke and semi-coke of coal, lignite or peat) and are not added. Customs coke is not in the coal tables above, whose code list is the coal codes only, and the coal lanes do not hold it: the coke lanes are listed apart.

Mozambique's exports under this code are left out of the coke tables, lanes, passage estimates, history and totals of the commodity pages and of the commodity blocks of the country pages, in each of the 16 years 2005 to 2024 in which the customs file records them (1.63 Mt in 2024, 4 destinations): the EIA series of coke production gives Mozambique none in any year, so its exports under the coke code are probably coal declared as coke; this is a hypothesis, not established (EIA International Energy Data: its coke production series reads 0 in every year from 1980 to 2025 (its coke export series reads 33 kt in 2023 and 0 in the other years); the same file gives it 6.5 Mt of metallurgical coal exports in 2025). The all-goods list of the country page of Mozambique shows the customs value of heading 2704 as declared. These rows are not counted: the tables and totals of this group are the customs file less them.

Australia, 2024: Queensland producers' sales to export of metallurgical coal by first destination, 137.0 Mt to 31 countries (hard coking 91.9 Mt, semi-soft coking 10.5 Mt, PCI 34.6 Mt), the sum of the four quarters of 2024, from the Queensland Government's Quarterly Coal Sales (CC BY 4.0). Credit as the workbook's About sheet gives it: "Source: Department of Natural Resources and Mines, Manufacturing and Regional and Rural Development (NRMMRRD)". PCI, pulverised coal for injection, is counted as metallurgical; before 2022 the file holds it inside semi-soft coking coal. The workbook is downloaded by hand and is not refreshed by the scheduled updates: it reads "Data through to 30 June 2026" and "Current as at October 2026", and its About sheet says that the data may be revised. The figures are the atlas's sums of the quarters. The disclaimer of the About sheet reads: "NRMMRRD has made a reasonable effort to ensure that the provided data is accurate and complete at the time of publishing. This information reflects data as reported to the Department and is a true and accurate representation of the data received. Authenticated information is only accurate as of the point in time of validation and verification. The Department is not responsible for data that is misrepresented, misinterpreted or altered in any way. Derived conclusions and analysis generated from this data are not to be considered attributable to the Department." Queensland's total of 2025: 131.5 Mt.

Queensland loads this coal at Gladstone Port 43.3 Mt, Dalrymple Bay 41.6 Mt, Hay Point 36.9 Mt and Abbot Point 15.2 Mt in 2024 (the file names Hay Point and Dalrymple Bay as two ports). The Queensland file gives the port of loading in total and the destination in total: it has no port by destination.

United States, 2024: exports of rank metallurgical as declared at export (U.S. Census Bureau, Monthly Report EM 545) to 34 countries, 51.3 Mt (56.59 million short tons at 0.90718474 t per short ton), from EIA's file of coal exports; 32 of the 34 countries have at least 1,000 t and are listed above. The file does not define the rank. By customs district, as the file names them: Norfolk, VA 30.1 Mt, Mobile, AL 8.76 Mt, Baltimore, MD 8.70 Mt, Buffalo, NY 2.18 Mt, New Orleans, LA 1.18 Mt; of the 2.56 Mt to Canada, 2.18 Mt left through Buffalo, NY, and the districts of this pair include Cleveland, OH and Detroit, MI, ports of the Great Lakes (the file does not say by which mode each district's coal left). The file is dated 1 October 2026; its description says that the figures of the latest period are preliminary estimates, final by the fall that follows the year (the file's latest year is 2025). Source: U.S. Energy Information Administration.

First destination is not always the buyer: 7 of the 31 Queensland pairs and 7 of the 32 United States pairs are above the customs record of all coal for the same pair in 2024; the largest gap is Australia to Singapore, 1.66 Mt against 0.14 Mt in customs data. The flows above are not a part of the customs flows of the Thermal coal page and are not subtracted from them: for Australia to India the customs data record 58.2 Mt of all coal and Queensland 35.4 Mt of metallurgical coal, and the difference (22.8 Mt) is not the thermal coal of that pair.

What these flows cover, 2024: EIA International gives metallurgical coal exports of 171.1 Mt for Australia and 51.3 Mt for the United States, of 370.8 Mt in the world. The Queensland rows are 80% of the Australian figure (New South Wales has no destinations in the Queensland file), the EIA rows 100% of the United States figure. No free source loaded gives destinations for Mongolia (56.4 Mt), Russia (37.1 Mt), Canada (28.9 Mt) and Mozambique (9.58 Mt), and no list of metallurgical coal of the atlas holds their coal by pair. Customs data give it for all types of coal together, in the places below: the flows of the Thermal coal page are the 20 largest customs pairs, and the lane tables of both coal pages (Seaborne lanes, group "Coal (all types)") list the customs lanes by sea. Mongolia: 1 of the 20 Main flows of the Thermal coal page (China 82.9 Mt); Russia: 4 of the 20 Main flows of the Thermal coal page (China 95.1 Mt, India 26.9 Mt, Turkey 24.4 Mt and 1 more) and 10 lanes of the lane tables of both coal pages; Canada: 5 lanes of the lane tables of both coal pages; Mozambique: 4 lanes of the lane tables of both coal pages.

Three definitions of metallurgical coal are on this page and are not added to one another: the tables above are EIA International, 2025, whole countries, all destinations; the Queensland rows are sales by Queensland producers with PCI included; the United States rows are exports by rank as declared. The flows are those of 2024, the year of the customs data, beside tables of 2025.
The seaborne lanes of this page are customs data for all coal, and coke: they are not the flows above.
Exports/imports tables are EIA metallurgical coal (not BACI).

Coke and semi-coke of coal, lignite or peat (HS 270400): the tables hold 32.9 Mt, 95% of the 34.6 Mt that the customs file records for these codes in 2024 (gross weight). The difference: 0.059 Mt are pairs under the threshold of the extract (1,000 t and USD 1 million; 358 of the 859 pairs of the file are kept); 1.63 Mt are the exports of Mozambique, left out as a misclassification (rule 5 of the cleaning rules: the EIA series of coke production gives Mozambique none in any year, so its exports under the coke code are probably coal declared as coke; this is a hypothesis, not established).

Customs data record 0.893 Mt of coke and semi-coke exported from Zimbabwe in 2024 (CEPII BACI, HS 2704), 2.7% of the world total. The EIA table of metallurgical coke production on the Metallurgical coal page gives Zimbabwe no coke production in 2025 (its series reads 0 in 2025, and its last two years with production are 399 kt in 2022 and 5 kt in 2023; EIA International Energy Data). Two readings fit, with the same weight: the EIA series no longer covers the country's coke plants (a series that falls from 399 kt to 5 kt and then to nothing may be a series that stopped), or part of these tonnes is another product declared under the coke code, metallurgical coal for instance, of which the EIA tables of the Metallurgical coal page give Zimbabwe a production of 1.25 Mt in 2025 and no exports. Neither is established here.
